preamble: In a Playfair word square the code phrase (in which no letter recurs) is followed by the remaining letters of the alphabet, I doing double duty for I and J. To encode a word it must first be split into pairs of letters, e.g. CR IT IC AL. Each pair is then to be seen as forming the diagonally opposite corners of a rectangle within the word square, the other two corners being the encoded form. Thus, in the example shown, CR gives SG (not GS, which RC would give). Where a pair of letters appears in the same row or column in the word square, its encoded form is produced from the letter immediately to the right of or below each respectively. For the last letter in a row or column the first letter in the same row or column becomes the encoded form. Thus IC becomes CE. When all the pairs are encoded, the word is joined up again, thus CRITICAL is encoded as SGCICEOP. The answers to the four asterisked clues, which are without definitions, must be encoded in the diagram. The code phrase (of two words, one of them an abbreviation) describes the answers to the asterisked clues. It must be deduced with the help of the answers to normal clues, so that the diagram may be completed.
